title: Progressive output guardrails and resilient function-call handoff acceptance
creator: Sofia Patel
description: This ticket defines the acceptance criteria and scope clarifications for a progressive (incremental) structured-output streaming protocol paired with robust function/tool call handoff semantics. Goal: provide deterministic, observable, and recoverable behaviors for streaming JSON-like payloads and tool invocation boundaries so downstream consumers (SDKs, gateways, and customer integrations) can rely on partial emissions, resume, and safe retries without risking duplicate side effects. Scope includes schema envelope design, framing and checkpoints, backpressure semantics, timeouts and retry policies, and mapping of error modes to graceful fallbacks. Implementation work will be coordinated with runtime, SDK, and console teams and must include instrumentation for traces and per-token telemetry for regressions testing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Schema handshake: The response stream MUST begin with a single machine-parseable metadata frame that includes: schema_version, model_variant, invocation_id, and optional expected_checkpoints array. SDKs can use invocation_id for idempotency and resume. Handshake frame must be validated by e2e tests.

2) Framed partial emits: All emitted payloads are framed JSON envelopes (type: 'partial'|'checkpoint'|'final'|'error'|'tool_call') with a monotonic frame_index. Consumers can assemble partials in order; out-of-order frames are marked and discarded by default unless explicit reordering is requested.

3) Checkpointing and resume: The runtime MUST emit checkpoint frames at configurable intervals (default every 256 tokens). A resumed stream with the same invocation_id and last_checkpoint_index should resume from after the checkpoint without re-emitting earlier partials.

4) Tool-call handshake & idempotency: Tool_call frames must include tool_id, call_args_digest, and call_id. The platform guarantees at-least-once delivery to tool backends; idempotency is achieved via call_id and call_args_digest. If a retry is issued, the tool gateway must detect duplicate call_id and return cached result or a deterministic error (409/duplicate).

5) Error taxonomy and fallback: Errors are classified as recoverable_stream (e.g., transient kernel OOM), fatal_stream (irrecoverable model context loss), tool_failure (tool-side error), and client_input_error. Each error frame must include suggested fallback: retry, fallback_model, or abort. SDKs and Console must surface the suggestion and trace.

6) Backpressure policy: When runtime is under load, it will emit backpressure frames with recommended_delay_ms. SDKs should honor recommended_delay_ms for client-side pacing; when delays exceed configured SLO (default 250ms), the system will either switch to a faster model variant or return a degraded but safe final frame according to rollout policy.

7) Streaming-to-synchronous fallback: If a client requests streaming but the runtime cannot sustain streaming SLOs for the invocation, the platform must transparently fallback to synchronous final-response mode and emit a terminal frame of type 'final' explaining the fallback_reason.

8) Observability & telemetry: Every invocation must emit structured telemetry events for handshake, checkpoints, each tool_call, each error frame, and finalization. Events must include invocation_id, frame_index, model_variant, and node_id. Dashboards and alert rules will use these events to detect regressions within 5 minutes of occurrence.

9) Deterministic partial ordering for persisted outputs: When customers opt-in to persist partial emissions (e.g., for incremental UI), the platform must guarantee deterministic ordering based on frame_index and checkpoint anchors across retries and restarts.

10) Security and provenance: All frames that contain tool_call results marked as 'sensitive' must be signed with a per-tenant KMS key fingerprint and include provenance metadata (requestor, timestamp, node_id). Audit logs must record tool_call success/failure with call_id.

11) Backwards compatibility: Clients that do not implement handshake parsing must continue to receive a valid final text payload. The runtime will include a compatibility text field in the 'final' frame for legacy clients until 2026-09-30.

12) Performance SLOs: Under standard load test (see test plan), 95th percentile latency to first partial frame must be <= 180ms for hosted tier and <= 120ms for dedicated tier when model_variant is labeled 'stream-optimized'.
test_plan: Unit: frame encoder/decoder tests for handshake, partial, checkpoint, error, tool_call, and final frames with fuzzed payloads.
Integration: end-to-end stream from SDK -> runtime -> tool_gateway with simulated transient failures, asserting idempotency via call_id and call_args_digest.
Resume tests: force process restart mid-stream and validate resume semantics using invocation_id and last_checkpoint_index.
Backpressure tests: synthetic overload scenarios to validate recommended_delay_ms is respected by SDK tests and that fallback to final mode triggers within SLO.
Chaos: network partitions between runtime and tool gateway and verify no silent duplicate side effects for retried tool_calls.
Performance: load tests for stream-optimized variants measuring 50/95/99 latency to first partial and token throughput.
Security: automated audit log replay tests verifying signed sensitive frames and KMS metadata are present and verifiable.
QA acceptance: manual review checklist for Console UX showing progressive partials, checkpoint markers, and linked tool_call traces in Logs view.
Canary rollout: 5% of traffic routed to new framing implementation for 48 hours with automatic rollback on error-rate > 0.5% or telemetry regressions per dashboard thresholds.
decision_log: Adopted a framed JSON envelope approach rather than an interleaved newline-delimited strategy to make tooling and parsing explicit and robust.
Checkpoints chosen as default every 256 tokens to balance resume granularity and overhead; this is configurable per-tenant.
Idempotency relies on a platform-supplied call_id plus call_args_digest to detect duplicates; implementing at-least-once delivery with de-dup in gateway avoids changing third-party tools.
Backpressure signaling uses recommended_delay_ms so SDKs can do adaptive pacing; runtime can decide to route to cheaper variants instead of immediate failure.
Compatibility plan: include compatibility text in final frames and deprecate legacy behavior with clear sunset date in release notes.
Opted to require security_review for signed sensitive frames and KMS integration; this will go through Security & Compliance sprint 2026-03.
